chunks: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from Ismāʿīl ibn Mihrān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan al-Marwazī, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said:
I was with Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he was asked: “Is there an addition in the supererogatory prayers during the month of Ramaḍān?” He said: “Yes.”

The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم used to pray after al-ʿatamah in his place of prayer and pronounce the takbīr, and the people would gather behind him to pray with his prayer. So when they pronounced takbīr behind him, he left them and entered his house.

Then when the people dispersed, he returned to his place of prayer and prayed as he had been praying. Then when the people pronounced takbīr behind him, he left them and went inside, and he did that repeatedly.

key_terms.الْعَتَمَةِ: the night prayer time after darkness, referring to ʿIshāʾ time

ai.seo_question: Did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم lead the people in extra nightly prayers during Ramaḍān?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that there was an increase in supererogatory prayer during the month of Ramaḍān. It also recounts the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, who would pray at night, but when people gathered behind him, he would leave and return only after they dispersed, repeating this several times.
